question: In the context of Mathura school of Art, during which of the following periods were a number of sculptures of Brahmanical deities, such as Kartikeya, Vishnu and Kubera carved?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Kushana**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__

• The Mathura school of art flourished during the period of the **Kushana dynasty**, particularly under the rule of emperors like Kanishka and Huvishka.

• This period saw the creation of numerous sculptures of Brahmanical deities including **Kartikeya, Vishnu, and Kubera**.

• Mathura art is known for its **red sandstone sculptures** and its distinctive style which combined indigenous Indian art forms with elements from Greek and Persian art.

• The Kushana period is significant for the development of **iconography** in Indian art, particularly the depiction of deities in human form.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Mathura School of Art:**

• The Mathura school is one of the major schools of Indian art which developed in the region of Mathura in Uttar Pradesh during the early centuries of the Common Era.

• It is renowned for its **sculptures in red sandstone**, which depict both religious and secular themes.

• The art from this school is characterized by **voluptuous forms, smiling faces, and elaborate headdresses**.

• Mathura was a significant center of artistic activity and production during ancient India.

• **Kushana Empire:**

• The Kushana Empire was a syncretic empire, formed by the Yuezhi in the Bactrian territories in the early 1st century CE, which reached its peak under the rule of Kanishka.

• The Kushanas played a crucial role in the development of the Silk Road trade network, connecting the East and the West.

• They were patrons of art and culture, and their period is marked by significant advancements in these fields.

• Under the Kushanas, especially Kanishka, the Gandhara school of art also flourished alongside the Mathura school.

• **Brahmanical Deities:**

• Brahmanical deities refer to the gods and goddesses worshipped in Brahmanism, the early form of Hinduism.

• Deities such as **Kartikeya (the god of war), Vishnu (the preserver), and Kubera (the god of wealth)** were commonly depicted in sculptures and iconography.

• The worship and representation of these deities became more standardized during the Kushana period, contributing to the development of Hindu iconography.
